title: Type annotation mismatch in sub-dependencies example (query_extractor may return None)
body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I'm @tiangolo or he asked me directly to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

Hi! First of all, thank you for the excellent documentation.

I noticed what appears to be a type annotation inconsistency in the **"Use the dependency"** example:

https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/sub-dependencies/#use-the-dependency

The first dependency is defined as:

```python
def query_extractor(q: str | None = None):
    return q
```

Since `q` is annotated as `str | None`, this function can return either a `str` or `None`.

Later, its return value is injected into the `q` parameter of another dependency:

```python
def query_or_cookie_extractor(
    q: Annotated[str, Depends(query_extractor)],
    last_query: Annotated[str | None, Cookie()] = None,
):
    if not q:
        return last_query
    return q
```

Here, `q` is annotated as `str`, but `query_extractor()` may return `None`.

For example, if a request is made without the `q` query parameter:

```http
GET /items/
```

then FastAPI will effectively resolve the dependencies like this:

```python
query_extractor(q=None)
# returns None

query_or_cookie_extractor(
    q=None,
    last_query=...
)
```

In other words, `q` may actually receive `None` at runtime, even though it is annotated as `str`.

The implementation itself seems to acknowledge this possibility:

```python
if not q:
    return last_query
```

This condition would only be necessary if `q` could be missing, empty, or `None`.

Because of that, wouldn't the following annotation be more accurate?

```python
def query_or_cookie_extractor(
    q: Annotated[str | None, Depends(query_extractor)],
    last_query: Annotated[str | None, Cookie()] = None,
):
    if not q:
        return last_query
    return q
```

This would make the type annotation consistent with the actual return type of the dependency and may help avoid confusion for users learning dependency injection or using static type checkers.

If there is an intentional reason for annotating `q` as `str`, I would appreciate any clarification.

Thanks again for the great documentation!

title: app.frontend() with fallback="index.html" returns 404 for client side routes that have a dot in the last path segment (like /users/john.doe or /v/1.2.3)
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/15979
Originally posted by **UditDewan** July 12, 2026 ### First Check - [x] I added a very descriptive title here. - [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [x] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [x] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [x] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [x] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Pydantic. - [x] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Swagger UI. - [x] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to ReDoc. ### Commit to Help - [x] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python import os import tempfile from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.testclient import TestClient dist = tempfile.mkdtemp() with open(os.path.join(dist, "index.html"), "w") as f: f.write("SPA shell") app = FastAPI() app.frontend("/", directory=dist, fallback="index.html") client = TestClient(app) # The Accept header a browser sends on a normal top level navigation. browser_nav = { "accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9," "image/avif,image/webp,image/apng,*/*;q=0.8" } print(client.get("/users/john", headers=browser_nav).status_code) # 200, serves index.html print(client.get("/users/john.doe", headers=browser_nav).status_code) # 404 print(client.get("/v/1.2.3", headers=browser_nav).status_code) # 404 ``` ### Description Hi 👋 I have been trying out the new `app.frontend()` helper to serve a single page app, using `fallback="index.html"` so that client side routes fall back to the shell and the frontend router can take over. This is the behavior described in the "Client side routing" part of the docs, and it works fine for a path like `/dashboard` or `/dashboard/settings`. The problem shows up when a client side route has a dot in its last path segment. Plenty of real apps have these, for example a profile at `/users/john.doe`, a version deep link at `/v/1.2.3`, or a slug like `/files/report.2024`. When I open one of those directly, or just hit refresh while I am already on that page, I get a 404 instead of the `index.html` shell, so the app never loads and the client router never gets a chance to handle the route. The part that surprised me is that setting `fallback="index.html"` explicitly does not change this. As far as I can tell there is currently no way to get these routes to fall back to the shell. I spent some time reading the code and I think it comes from `_is_frontend_navigation_request()` in `fastapi/routing.py`. It takes the last path segment and if `os.path.splitext(...)` finds an extension it returns early and treats the request as an asset request, before it ever looks at the `Accept` header. Because `os.path.splitext("john.doe")` returns `.doe`, any segment with a dot in it is treated as a file and never gets the `index.html` fallback, even when the browser clearly asked for `text/html`. What makes me think this is fixable without regressions is that the two situations are easy to tell apart. A real browser navigation sends `Accept: text/html`, while a missing asset requested from a script tag, an image tag, or a fetch call sends `*/*` or a specific type like `text/css`. If I request a genuinely missing asset such as `/assets/missing.js` with `Accept: */*` it still returns 404 as expected, so checking the `Accept` header first would fix the navigation case and keep the asset case working. I did notice there is already a test that pins the current behavior. `test_index_fallback_does_not_handle_asset_like_or_non_html_requests` has a `("/users/jane.doe", "text/html")` case that expects a 404, so before proposing a change I wanted to ask whether the current behavior is intentional. If the idea is that dotted client routes should be servable, would a change that treats an explicit `Accept: text/html` request as navigation regardless of the path be acceptable? Or would you rather keep the extension heuristic as the default for `fallback="auto"` and add an opt in for apps that use dotted client side routes? I am happy to open a PR with a failing test and the change for whichever direction you prefer. Thanks a lot for the work on this feature. ### Operating System Windows ### Operating System Details Also reproduced on current master. The logic involved is pure routing code, so it is not tied to any particular operating system. ### FastAPI Version 0.139.0 ### Pydantic Version 2.13.4 ### Python Version 3.11 ### Additional Context _No response_

title: Race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild can 404 valid routes and permanently corrupt the candidate cache
body:
### Description

Since the router refactor in 0.137.0 (#15745), `_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates()` and `_IncludedRouter.effective_low_priority_routes()` in `fastapi/routing.py` rebuild their cached lists lazily on first use, with no synchronization.

The rebuild publishes an empty list on the shared attribute first, appends routes into it one by one, and only stamps the version at the end:

```python
self._effective_candidates = []
# ... appends into self._effective_candidates in a loop ...
self._effective_candidates_version = routes_version
```

If several threads drive the app's first requests at the same time (for example per-thread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any embedding that serves one app object from multiple event loops), more than one thread can pass the version check and rebuild concurrently. Every rebuilder appends into whichever list was assigned to the attribute last, so the cache ends up with duplicated candidates, and the corruption is permanent because the version gets stamped anyway. A request that runs while the list is still partially built can also get a 404 for a route that exists.

The rebuild path additionally uses `warnings.catch_warnings()` internally (via response field construction), so interleaved rebuilds can leak entries into the global warnings filters.

### Reproduction

```python
import sys
import threading

from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from fastapi.routing import _IncludedRouter
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

N_ROUTES = 120
N_THREADS = 6

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
for i in range(N_ROUTES):
    def endpoint(i: int = i):
        return {"i": i}
    router.add_api_route(f"/r{i}", endpoint, methods=["GET"])
app.include_router(router)

sys.setswitchinterval(1e-5)  # widen the rebuild window
barrier = threading.Barrier(N_THREADS)

def worker():
    client = TestClient(app)
    barrier.wait()
    client.get(f"/r{N_ROUTES - 1}")

threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(N_THREADS)]
for t in threads:
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()

included = next(r for r in app.router.routes if isinstance(r, _IncludedRouter))
print(len(included._effective_candidates), "cached candidates, expected", N_ROUTES)
```

On my machine this reliably prints around 600 cached candidates for the 120 route app.

### Expected behavior

The cache rebuild should be thread safe. Building the list into a local variable and publishing it atomically (list first, version second) keeps readers from ever seeing a partial list, and serializing the rebuild avoids the duplicated appends and the warnings filter leak.

### Environment

- FastAPI version: 0.139.0
- Python version: 3.14.5
- OS: Windows 11

Related report: discussion #15914 describes the same symptoms.

title: Named type alias body loses OpenAPI ref
body:
### Description

FastAPI generates different OpenAPI schemas for a bare named Pydantic type alias and the same alias wrapped in `Annotated[..., Body()]`.

This came up while discussing the Pydantic side in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13236.

Example:

```py
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from fastapi import Body, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

app = FastAPI()


class Cat(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal["cat"]
    meows: int


class Dog(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal["dog"]
    barks: float


class Lizard(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal["reptile", "lizard"]
    scales: bool


type Pet = Annotated[
    Cat | Dog | Lizard,
    Field(discriminator="pet_type"),
]


@app.post("/bare")
def bare(pet: Pet):
    return pet


@app.post("/body")
def body(pet: Annotated[Pet, Body()]):
    return pet
```

Expected: both routes should generate the same request-body schema shape, with a named `Pet` component:

```json
{
  "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Pet"
}
```

Actual: `/body` references `#/components/schemas/Pet`, but `/bare` emits the discriminated union schema inline in the request body.

### Why this matters

For normal `BaseModel` request bodies, FastAPI supports the ergonomic form:

```py
def create_item(item: Item):
    ...
```

A named discriminated union is also a valid Pydantic body type, but today it needs the more verbose form to get the same named OpenAPI component behavior:

```py
def create_pet(pet: Annotated[Pet, Body()]):
    ...
```

`RootModel` is not a good workaround because it adds a `.root` wrapper, while the desired request body is the flat union object itself.

### Suggested fix

FastAPI should preserve the named alias when it auto-infers a body parameter.

It looks like FastAPI currently unwraps `TypeAliasType` / PEP 695 aliases during parameter analysis. That may be useful for deciding whether the parameter is a body/query parameter, but the original alias should still be used when creating the inferred body field.

So this:

```py
def create_pet(pet: Pet):
    ...
```

should produce the same OpenAPI request-body schema as:

```py
def create_pet(pet: Annotated[Pet, Body()]):
    ...
```

title: 0.137.0: `APIRoute.tags` invisible to type checkers in generate_unique_id_function (regression from #15745)
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/15749
Originally posted by **tedserbinski** June 15, 2026 ### First check - I searched existing discussions and issues — no existing report for this. - This is about a **type-checker regression in 0.137.0**, not a runtime bug (runtime is unaffected). ### Summary In **0.137.0**, the documented `generate_unique_id_function` pattern from [Advanced → Generate Clients](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/generate-clients/) — which reads `route.tags` — now fails static type checking. Type checkers report that `APIRoute` has no attribute `tags`, even though the docs still show exactly this code and it works fine at runtime. This appears to be an unintended side-effect of #15745 ("Refactor internals to preserve APIRouter and APIRoute instances"): `APIRoute.__init__` was changed to delegate state-setting to a helper that receives `self` cast to the `_APIRouteLike` Protocol, and `APIRoute` itself no longer carries a class-level `tags` annotation. So the attribute is still assigned at runtime, but it's invisible to type checkers looking at the `APIRoute` type. ### Reproducible example This is the docs' own example (`docs_src/generate_clients/tutorial003_py310.py`): ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.routing import APIRoute def custom_generate_unique_id(route: APIRoute) -> str: return f"{route.tags[0]}-{route.name}" app = FastAPI(generate_unique_id_function=custom_generate_unique_id) ``` Running a type checker (`ty`) over it on 0.137.0: ``` error[unresolved-attribute]: Object of type `APIRoute` has no attribute `tags` --> repro.py:6:15 | 6 | return f"{route.tags[0]}-{route.name}" | ^^^^^^^^^^ ``` At runtime the same code builds the app and generates operation IDs correctly — only the static type surface is affected. `route.name` resolves fine; only `route.tags` is missing. ### Expected behavior `route.tags` should remain visible to type checkers as a public attribute of `APIRoute` (it's part of the documented public callback contract), as it was in 0.136.x where `APIRoute.__init__` assigned `self.tags = tags or []` directly. ### Environment - FastAPI: **0.137.0** - Python: 3.14 - Type checker: `ty` 0.0.49 (also reproduces with strict Pyright per the same root cause); mypy may differ - OS: macOS ### Possible fix Add the lost class-level annotation back to `APIRoute` (e.g. `tags: list[str | Enum]`) so it matches what the `_APIRouteLike` Protocol already declares. Happy to open a PR if that direction is welcome. Thanks for FastAPI! 🙏

title: 0.137.0: empty-path route nested under prefix-less outer include raises 'Prefix and path cannot be both empty'
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/15750
Originally posted by **yeonghun-toggle** June 15, 2026 ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, APIRouter leaf = APIRouter() @leaf.get("") # empty path def list_items(): return [] inner = APIRouter() inner.include_router(leaf, prefix="/items") # inner include HAS a prefix app = FastAPI() app.include_router(inner) # outer include has NO prefix ``` ### Description On **0.137.0**, the last line raises at app-construction time: `fastapi.exceptions.FastAPIError: Prefix and path cannot be both empty (path operation: list_items)` On **0.136.3** and earlier the same code works and registers the route at `/items`. This is a regression introduced by the route-tree refactor in #15745 (preserving `APIRouter`/`APIRoute` instances instead of flattening on include). It only happens when an empty-path route (`path=""`) is nested **and** at least one include hop in its ancestry has no prefix. If every hop carries a prefix it still works on 0.137.0. Verified on both versions: | setup | 0.136.3 | 0.137.0 | |---|---|---| | `app.include_router(leaf, prefix="/items")` (single include) | `/items` | works | | `inner` and `app` both include with a prefix | `/v1/items` | works | | `inner` has prefix, `app.include_router(inner)` has no prefix | `/items` | **raises** | ### Operating System macOS ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.137.0 ### Pydantic Version 2.13.4 ### Python Version 3.12.13 ### Additional Context Root-cause pointer (from a quick read of 0.137.0 `fastapi/routing.py`): in `include_router`, when `prefix` is empty, it recursively iterates the included route candidates and raises if any route's **raw** `path` is empty — without composing the prefixes contributed by the intermediate included routers. So a leaf that was included with a prefix at an inner hop still trips the check at a prefix-less outer include. Whether the right fix is to validate the **effective** (prefix-composed) path, or to defer this validation to route-resolution time, is a design call for the refactor author.

title: Implement GraphQL integration with automatic schema generation from Pydantic models

FastAPI excels at REST but lacks GraphQL support. GraphQL schema must be defined separately from Pydantic models. Code duplication between REST and GraphQL definitions. Teams choose between REST and GraphQL instead of offering both.

**Business Impact:** Enables flexible querying, supports multiple client needs, improves API flexibility, enables modern frontend patterns.

## Root Cause Analysis
GraphQL is separate from REST. Schema duplication is required. Integration is manual.

## Solution Overview
- Create FastAPI-GraphQL integration
- Auto-generate GraphQL schema from Pydantic
- Support both REST and GraphQL simultaneously
- Build query validation
- Add performance monitoring

**Implementation Steps:**

2. Build schema generator from Pydantic
3. Implement query resolver system
4. Add authentication/authorization
5. Create examples and documentation

title: SSE `stream_item_type` not propagated through `APIRouter` + `include_router`
body:
### Summary

When an SSE route (`response_class=EventSourceResponse` + `AsyncIterator[Frame]` return annotation) is defined on an `APIRouter` and then merged onto a `FastAPI` app via `include_router`, the resulting merged route loses its `stream_item_type`. As a consequence, the OpenAPI `text/event-stream` response schema omits the `data.contentSchema`, so tooling like `datamodel-codegen` cannot generate frame models.

Defining the same route directly on the `FastAPI` app via `@app.post(...)` works correctly.

### Reproduction

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Frame(BaseModel):
    kind: str


# Case A — route registered directly on the app: works
app_a = FastAPI()

@app_a.post("/s", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
async def a() -> AsyncIterator[Frame]:
    yield Frame(kind="x")


# Case B — route defined on a router, then `include_router`: broken
router = APIRouter()

@router.post("/s", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
async def b() -> AsyncIterator[Frame]:
    yield Frame(kind="x")


app_b = FastAPI()
app_b.include_router(router)

print("DIRECT:", app_a.routes[-1].stream_item_type)
print("ROUTER (pre-include):", router.routes[-1].stream_item_type)
print("APP (post-include):", app_b.routes[-1].stream_item_type)


def has_content_schema(spec: dict) -> bool:
    sse = spec["paths"]["/s"]["post"]["responses"]["200"]["content"]["text/event-stream"]
    return "contentSchema" in sse.get("itemSchema", {}).get("properties", {}).get("data", {})


print("DIRECT openapi has contentSchema:", has_content_schema(app_a.openapi()))
print("INCLUDE_ROUTER openapi has contentSchema:", has_content_schema(app_b.openapi()))
```

Output:

```
DIRECT: <class '__main__.Frame'>
ROUTER (pre-include): <class '__main__.Frame'>
APP (post-include): None

DIRECT openapi has contentSchema: True
INCLUDE_ROUTER openapi has contentSchema: False
```

### Expected

After `include_router`, the merged route on `app_b` should carry the same `stream_item_type` as the source route, and the emitted OpenAPI should include the `contentSchema` under `responses.200.content["text/event-stream"].itemSchema.properties.data` referencing `Frame`.

### Actual

The merged route's `stream_item_type` is `None`; the emitted OpenAPI shows the generic SSE envelope (`data: string, event, id, retry`) with no `contentSchema`.

### Root cause (proposed)

In `fastapi/routing.py`, `APIRoute.__init__` populates `self.stream_item_type` only inside the branch guarded by `isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder)`:

```python
if isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder):
    return_annotation = get_typed_return_annotation(endpoint)
    if lenient_issubclass(return_annotation, Response):
        response_model = None
    else:
        stream_item = get_stream_item_type(return_annotation)
        if stream_item is not None:
            if (
                isinstance(response_class, DefaultPlaceholder)
                or lenient_issubclass(response_class, EventSourceResponse)
            ) and not lenient_issubclass(stream_item, ServerSentEvent):
                self.stream_item_type = stream_item
            response_model = None
        else:
            response_model = return_annotation
self.response_model = response_model
```

When the source route (on the `APIRouter`) is created, `response_model` starts as a `DefaultPlaceholder`, the detection runs, and `self.response_model` is overwritten to `None`.

`APIRouter.include_router` then creates the merged route with:

```python
self.add_api_route(
    prefix + route.path,
    route.endpoint,
    response_model=route.response_model,  # now None, not DefaultPlaceholder
    ...
    response_class=use_response_class,
    ...
)
```

On the merged route's `__init__`, `isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder)` is now `False`, so the detection branch is skipped and `self.stream_item_type` stays at its initial `None`.

The symmetric issue likely affects JSONL streaming (`response_class=DefaultPlaceholder` path) too, since it's gated by the same `DefaultPlaceholder` check on `response_model`.

### Suggested fix

Either:
1. In `include_router`, additionally copy `stream_item_type` onto the new route (simplest, closest to the current wiring).
2. In `APIRoute.__init__`, run stream-item detection regardless of whether `response_model` is a `DefaultPlaceholder`, as long as `response_model is None` after the conditional.

### Environment

- `fastapi==0.135.2`
- `pydantic==2.12.5`
- `starlette==1.0.0`
- Python `3.11.6`
- macOS 14.4.1

Happy to open a PR if the preferred fix direction is specified.

1) This leads to a loss of information regarding which fields have been explicitly set, since default values are now considered as having been provided.
12) Consequently, validation is enforced on default values, which might not be the intended behavior and anyway different from the one from json body.
